{# Page scaffold. A section registers itself as it renders, and the table of contents is built from what registered -- so a section id and its TOC entry cannot drift apart, and `section scrollspy` is spelled in exactly one place. Import these `with context`: they read `toc_sections` off the context. section(id, label) heading is the label section(id, label, heading=false) no heading (intro sections) section(id, label, heading="...") heading text differs from the TOC entry section(id, label, tag="h2") heading level other than h3 #} {% macro section(id, label, heading=None, tag="h3") %} {%- do toc_sections.append({'id': id, 'label': label}) -%} {%- set heading_role = {'h2': 'headline-large', 'h3': 'headline-medium', 'h4': 'title-large'}.get(tag, 'headline-medium') -%}
{%- if heading is not false %} <{{ tag }} class="docs-section-title {{ heading_role }}">{{ heading if heading is not none else label }} {%- endif %} {{ caller() }}
{% endmacro %} {# Extra, non-section entries (an off-site link, say) go in a {% call toc() %}. #} {% macro toc() %}
    {%- for s in toc_sections %}
  • {{ s.label }}
    • {%- endfor %} {{- caller() if caller }}
{% endmacro %} {# `toc_extra` is a macro rendering extra
  • s for the table of contents. #} {% macro page_body(toc_extra=None) %}
    {{ caller() }}
    {% if toc_extra %}{% call toc() %}{{ toc_extra() }}{% endcall %}{% else %}{{ toc() }}{% endif %}
    {% endmacro %} {# A code sample. Write the markup for real -- the macro escapes it -- instead of hand-typing < and >. Keep the body flush left: 
     preserves the
    indentation you give it.

    tests/semantics.test.js checks every one of these against SEMANTICS.md. A
    sample that deliberately shows non-conforming markup -- a migration
    before/after, say -- opts out with check=false and a reason:

        {% raw %}{% call code(check=false, reason="0.7.0 markup, shown for migration") %}{% endraw %}

    The reason is required; the test fails on a bare opt-out, so an exemption
    always says why it is still earned. Neither argument renders.
#}
